summary.short: A bill that, once enacted, would create an AI Authority, set AI regulatory principles, and provide by regulations for sandboxes, AI officers, training-data records, labelling and independent audits; the Act comes into force on the day it is passed.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill has the Secretary of State make regulations creating an AI Authority (s.1), with functions including coordinating regulators, reviewing legislation, monitoring AI risks, supporting sandboxes and accrediting independent AI auditors. Section 2 sets regulatory principles the Authority must have regard to. Section 3 requires it to construct regulatory sandboxes in which firms test innovative propositions with real consumers on a small scale. Section 4 requires, by regulations, that businesses developing, deploying or using AI designate an AI officer. Section 5 provides for regulations requiring persons training AI to record third-party data and IP used and to assure informed consent and copyright compliance; for AI product or service suppliers to give health warnings, labelling and consent opportunities; and for businesses to allow accredited independent auditors to audit their systems. Section 7 defines AI, including generative AI. Section 8 allows regulations to create offences, fees, penalties and fines. The Act extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland and comes into force on the day it is passed.

relations.note: Section 4(2) inserts a new item (iv) after paragraph (iii) of section 414C(7)(b), covering AI development, deployment or use by the company and the AI officer designated under this Act.

notes: Bill text as introduced; the document gives no version stamp and registry status is pending. Most operative duties (sections 1(1), 3(1), 4(1), 5(1)) are delegated to regulations with no dates stated. Section 5(1)(a)(iii) and (iv) are numbered under the training-data paragraph (a) but concern product or service suppliers and businesses, so the structure is ambiguous. Stray line-number artefacts appear in the text ('40' in section 3(2), '35' in section 5(1)). Section 4(2) refers to this Act by its own short title; no other instrument is stated as legal basis. Section 8(2) allows offences, fees, penalties and fines, but the bill sets none itself.

thresholds.note: The bill sets no numeric cutoffs that change legal treatment. Scope is defined without numbers ('any business which develops, deploys or uses AI' in sections 4 and 5, 'any person involved in training AI' in section 5(1)(a)). Numbers in the text are section and subsection references (e.g., section 5(1)(a)(iv), section 414C(7)(b)) or stray line numbers ('40', '35'), not thresholds. Size or performance tiers are not present; the Secretary of State may later amend sections 1, 2, 3 and 4 by regulations, but no delegated numeric threshold is stated.
